questions.question: ____ are used to warn others about hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Placards are diamond-shaped signs placed on packages and vehicles to warn drivers and others about hazardous materials. The shipper must place them correctly. The driver must check that they are correct.

questions.question: Many products classified as poison are also:
questions.explanation: Many poisonous hazardous materials are also flammable.

questions.question: Before loading or unloading flammable liquids, the engine must be:
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before loading or unloading flammable liquids. The only exception is if you need to run the engine to operate a pump.

questions.question: A driver needs a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to transport hazardous materials in:

options.text: A vehicle requiring a Class A license.
A vehicle requiring a Class B license.
A vehicle requiring a Class C license.

questions.explanation: You must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle that carries hazardous materials, regardless of size.

questions.question: The only proper way to check tire pressure is by:

options.text: Pushing on the tires to feel the pressure.

questions.explanation: Check each tire at the start of every trip. A tire pressure gauge is the only way to accurately measure tire pressure.

questions.question: Shipping papers should be:

options.text: Easily seen by anyone entering the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Easily seen by anyone entering the cab.
questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's side door or in another location you can reach while wearing your seat belt. They must be easy to see for anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: Column 2 of the Hazardous Materials Table contains:
questions.explanation: Column 2 of the Hazardous Materials Table lists the proper shipping names and descriptions of regulated materials.

questions.question: A person must not smoke within ____ of a vehicle placarded for Class 3 or Division 2.1 materials.
questions.explanation: Do not smoke within 25 feet of a placarded cargo tank carrying Class 3 or Division 2.1 hazardous materials.

questions.question: Emergency response information from the shipper must include:

options.text: Any risks of fire or explosion.
How many people should respond in case of an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any risks of fire or explosion.
questions.explanation: Emergency response information must include: basic descriptions and technical names of materials; health hazards; risks of fire or explosion; immediate precautions for accidents; how to handle fires; how to handle spills or leaks; and first aid steps.

questions.question: If transporting chlorine, what must be in the vehicle?
questions.explanation: When transporting chlorine in cargo tanks, the driver must have an approved gas mask in the vehicle.

questions.question: You are transporting Class 3 flammable liquids and need to move the cargo to another tank. What should you do?

options.text: You can transfer them on the road as long as no one else is nearby.
Do not transfer them on a public road unless it is an emergency.
Keep the transfer secret when moving them to another tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not transfer them on a public road unless it is an emergency.
questions.explanation: Never transfer flammable liquids from one vehicle to another on a public road unless there is an emergency. Always warn others about the hazards of these materials.

questions.question: If the letter "G" appears in Column 1 of a hazardous materials shipping paper, what else must be on the paper?

options.text: The technical name of the hazardous material.
The type of container holding the hazardous material.

questions.correctAnswerText: The technical name of the hazardous material.
questions.explanation: A "G" in Column 1 means the description in Column 2 is a generic name. A generic name must be paired with the technical name.

questions.question: While driving, where should shipping papers be kept?
questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a pouch in the driver's side door or in another place you can easily reach while wearing your seat belt. They must be easy to see for anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: You see a package of explosives with an oily stain or dampness. What should you do?

options.text: Use towels to absorb the liquid.

questions.explanation: Never transport damaged packages of explosives. Do not accept any package that appears damp or has an oily stain.

questions.question: What license do you need to drive a vehicle carrying hazardous materials?

options.text: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.
A CDL with a passenger endorsement.
A CDL with an air brake endorsement.

questions.correctAnswerText: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.
questions.explanation: You must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement before driving any vehicle that carries hazardous materials, even if it is not currently carrying them.

questions.question: Class 1, Class 2.1, and Class 3 materials should not be placed in a trailer with what?
questions.explanation: Cargo heaters are not always permitted. When transporting Class 1 (Explosives), Class 2.1 (Flammable Gas), or Class 3 (Flammable Liquids), heaters are usually prohibited.

questions.question: When you are seated in the driver's seat, where should shipping papers be?

options.text: Taped to the passenger's side window.

questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a pouch in the driver's side door or in another place you can easily reach while wearing your seat belt. They must be easy to see for anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: Shippers must label hazardous materials. If an item is too small for its label, how should it be labeled?

options.text: Tie it with other hazardous materials and label the outside bundle with paper.
Attach the label to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.
Mark it with a large orange dot.
Place it in a box that displays a warning label.

questions.correctAnswerText: Attach the label to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.
questions.explanation: Shippers must place diamond-shaped hazard warning labels on hazardous materials packages. If the label does not fit on the package, it can be placed on a tag that is securely attached to it.

questions.question: What do you need to know to choose the correct placards for hazardous materials?

options.text: The hazard classes of the materials.
The types of containers being used.

questions.correctAnswerText: The hazard classes of the materials.
questions.explanation: Placards are placed on the outside of a vehicle to show which hazard classes are being carried.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle, where should hazardous materials' shipping papers be kept?
questions.explanation: Shipping papers must always be easy to find. Leave them on the driver's seat when you are not in the vehicle.

questions.question: If you find that your cargo is leaking, what should you do?

options.text: Touch the leaking material to find out what it is.
Use shipping papers and labels to identify the leaking cargo.
Assume all of the cargo is leaking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use shipping papers and labels to identify the leaking cargo.
questions.explanation: If you find a leak in hazardous materials cargo, use the shipping papers, labels, or package location to identify what is leaking. Do not touch the leaking material.

questions.question: As a driver at an accident scene, which task is NOT your job?

options.text: Keep people away from the scene.
Try to put out a hazardous materials fire by yourself.
Tell emergency responders about the hazardous materials danger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Try to put out a hazardous materials fire by yourself.
questions.explanation: Your job as a driver is to keep people away, limit the spread of material if safe, tell emergency responders about the danger, and give them the shipping papers. Do not try to fight hazardous materials fires unless you have protective equipment and training.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with empty hazardous materials tanks, what must you do at railroad crossings?

options.text: Slow down, but you do not have to stop.

questions.explanation: A vehicle with hazardous materials tanks must always stop at railroad crossings before driving over them, even if the tanks are empty.

questions.question: Where should hazardous materials shipping papers NOT be kept?

options.text: In a pouch on the driver's door.
In a pouch on the passenger's door.
Within reach of the driver while the seat belt is fastened.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a pouch on the passenger's door.
questions.explanation: Shipping papers must be easy to get in an emergency. Keep them in a pouch on the driver's door or in clear view within reach while your seat belt is fastened. You can keep them on the driver's seat when you are not in the vehicle.

questions.question: What must be done with containers of hazardous materials?

options.text: Secure them so they do not move during transport.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure them so they do not move during transport.
questions.explanation: Secure containers so they will not fall, slide, or bounce during transportation. All hazardous materials packages must be secured.

questions.question: What should you NOT use when loading hazardous materials containers?
questions.explanation: Do not use hooks or any tools that could damage containers or packaging when loading or unloading hazardous materials.

questions.question: When refueling a vehicle with hazardous materials, what should you do?

options.text: Have someone other than the driver do it.

questions.explanation: Always turn off the engine before refueling a vehicle carrying hazardous materials. Someone must always watch the nozzle and control the fuel flow.

questions.question: When loading hazardous materials, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Load the materials away from heat.

questions.explanation: Do not use hooks or tools that could damage containers or packaging when loading hazardous materials.

questions.question: If you find hazardous materials leaking while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Keep driving to find a phone to call the National Response Center.
Leave the area to find help.

questions.explanation: If you discover leaking hazardous materials, park as soon as possible. Continuing to drive creates a longer trail of contamination, which endangers others and increases clean-up costs.

questions.question: When transporting hazardous materials, how should placards be used?

options.text: On all four sides of the vehicle.
Only by Class A licensed drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all four sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards must be placed on all four sides of any vehicle transporting hazardous materials.
